chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me: Ahmad and Abdullah, the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, narrated to me, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who said: I heard some of the trustworthy companions of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) say:

There is in this chest of mine a vast amount of knowledge which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught me. If I could find guardians for it who would preserve it as it deserves and transmit it as they hear it from me, I would have bequeathed some of it to them. Thus, much of the knowledge was known through it. Indeed, knowledge is the key to every door, and every door opens a thousand doors.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the hidden knowledge in Imam Ali's chest and the metaphor of knowledge as a key?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) alludes to the *Ilm al-Ladunni* (divine, specialized knowledge) stored in his chest, which he withheld due to the scarcity of worthy guardians (*huffaz*) capable of preserving its nuances. This highlights the Shia concept of the Ahl al-Bayt as the living repositories of the Prophet's esoteric and exoteric teachings, emphasizing that true knowledge is not merely informational but a transformative key that unlocks deeper layers of reality.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-19 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad and Abdullah - the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Abi Hamzih al-Somali, on the authority of Abi Ishaq al-Sabi’e, on the authority of one of the trustworthy companions of the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) that he had heard Ali (MGB) say, “

There is a lot of knowledge in my heart which God’s Prophet (MGB) has taught me. I would have taught it to others if I could have found people who were trustworthy enough. I would have taught them so that they may acquire some knowledge since this knowledge is the key to every gate and each gate opens up to another thousand gates.”
